items.prose: The opponent bets £40 into £80. You win 30% of the time.
items.question: What does calling earn on average, in £?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Weight the £120 win and the £40 loss by their chances.

byKey.pot: £24 is 30% of £80. The call wins £120 (the pot and his bet) and can lose £40.
byKey.price: You used the £80 pot as the win. A call wins the pot and his £40: £120.

explain.text: The price is $\tfrac{40}{160} = 25\%$. The call wins £120 with chance 0.3 and loses £40 otherwise: $36 - 28 = £8$.

items.prose: On the turn you hold an inside straight draw: 4 outs, 46 unseen cards, one card to come.
items.question: What is your chance of hitting, as a percentage?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide the outs by the unseen cards.

byKey.rule: 8% is the rule of two. The exact chance is $\tfrac{4}{46} = 8.70\%$.

explain.text: Four of 46 unseen cards complete the straight: 8.70%. The rule of two gives 8% as a check.

items.prose: On the flop you hold a flush draw and an inside straight draw. That is 12 outs among 47 unseen cards, two to come.
items.question: What is your chance of hitting by the river, as a percentage?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take the chance of no out on either card from 1.

byKey.four: 48% is the rule of four, which overstates big draws. The exact chance is 44.96%.
byKey.one: That is one card only, $\tfrac{12}{47}$. Two cards are to come.

explain.text: No out on either card has chance $\tfrac{35}{47} \cdot \tfrac{34}{46} = 0.5504$, so you hit 44.96% of the time. The rule of four says 48%, too high with this many outs.

items.prose: One jack is on the board.
items.question: How many combos of two jacks can your opponent hold?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count pairs from the jacks you cannot see.

byKey.six: Six is the count with no jack seen. One is on the board, leaving $\binom32$.

explain.text: Three jacks are unseen, so $\binom32 = 3$ combos.

items.prose: An ace is on the board and you hold a queen.
items.question: How many ace-queen combos can your opponent hold?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count his live aces and live queens.

byKey.twelve: 12 strikes out the ace on the board only. Your queen blocks too.
byKey.sixteen: 16 ignores both cards you can see.

explain.text: Three aces and three queens are live, so $3 \times 3 = 9$ combos. Your own queen is a blocker.

items.prose: On the river your opponent bets £60 into £120. A balanced bettor bluffs a quarter of the time at this size.
items.question: How often should you call, as a fraction?

byKey.half: Half fits a pot-sized bet. A half-pot bet must be called more often.
byKey.quarter: A quarter is his bluff share, not your calling frequency.

explain.text: His bluff risks £60 to win £120, so it breaks even when you call $\tfrac{120}{180} = \tfrac23$ of the time. Bluffs are $\tfrac{60}{240} = \tfrac14$ of his bets.

items.prose: An opponent calls only 30% of the time against pot-sized bets, say £100 into £100.
items.question: Should you bluff him?

options.why: They lose £100 when called, 30% of the time, but win £100 the other 70%.

options.text: Only half the time, to stay balanced
options.why: Balance protects you from an exploiter. He folds too often, so bluff every time you can.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out a bluff's average against him.

explain.text: A bluff wins the £100 pot when he folds, 70% of the time, and loses £100 when he calls. That is $70 - 30 = +£40$ a bluff. He should call half the time against this size.

items.prose: A trade makes £30 or loses £20, each with chance one half. An analyst calls it good or bad and is right 90% of the time.
items.question: What is the analyst worth, in £?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Value with the analyst, less the value now.

byKey.with: £12.50 is the value with the analyst. Take away the £5 you get anyway.
byKey.perfect: £10 is perfect information. A 90% analyst is worth less.

explain.text: After a good call the trade is worth $27 - 2 = £25$; after a bad one $3 - 18 = -£15$, so skip. With him $0.5 \times 25 = £12.50$, against £5 now: £7.50.

items.prose: A bet pays 3 to 1 and wins 30% of the time.
items.question: What is the Kelly fraction?

byKey.p: 0.3 is the win chance, not the stake.
byKey.even: You used even money, $2p - 1$. This bet pays 3 to 1.

explain.text: $f^* = 0.3 - \tfrac{0.7}{3} = 0.0667$. The edge is small, so the stake is small.

items.prose: Even-money bets won 55% of the time, £1 a bet, from a bankroll of £15, with no target.
items.question: What is the chance of ruin?

byKey.q: 0.45 is the chance of losing one bet. Ruin needs the bankroll to reach 0.
